meaning: to relax and feel comfortable as if you were in your own house
literal_translation: siéntete como en tu casa, relájate y ponte cómodo
example: Come in and make yourself at home. I will get you a drink.
origin: Said to welcome guests so they feel relaxed in your house

wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is about feeling comfortable and relaxed, not about cleaning or tidying a house.
The idiom does not mention buying or moving. It describes how a guest feels in a place.
This is the opposite of the idiom. When you make yourself at home, you stay and relax.

explanation: 'Make yourself at home' is a friendly phrase used to invite guests to relax. It means you can behave as comfortably as if you were in your own house.
